items.q: Leukocoria with calcified intraocular mass in a 2 year old is diagnostic of what?
o: Retinoblastoma needing staging with family screening
items.exp: Calcium within white mass separates tumour from Coats telangiectasia (no calcium, older boys) and cataract (lens opacity); gene testing with sibling EUAs follows urgently.
items.kp: Toddler white pupil with calcium: retinoblastoma.

items.q: Bilateral retinoblastoma implies which genetics and extra eye risk?
o: Heritable RB1 with pineal trilateral tumour risk and sibling screening
items.exp: Germline mutation seeds both eyes multifocally with pineoblastoma and second sarcomas; RB1 counselling with prenatal and sibling EUAs saves lives beyond the proband.
items.kp: Both eyes in toddler: RB1, scan pineal, screen sibs.

items.q: Collar button mushroom mass with orange lipofuscin in adult choroid is what?
items.exp: Bruch rupture crowns the tumour while low B scan reflectivity confirms; size and genetics set plaque versus enucleation while liver imaging schedules lifelong.
items.kp: Mushroom through Bruch in adult: melanoma.

items.q: Medium choroidal melanoma is most often treated eye sparingly by what?
items.exp: Radioactive plaques deliver apex dose preserving globe comparably to enucleation in COMS trials; large or nerve invading tumours still enucleate.
items.kp: Medium melanoma: sew on a plaque.

items.q: Creamy multiple choroidal lesions with exudative detachment in breast cancer patient are what?
o: Metastases treated via systemic therapy with palliative laser
items.exp: Bilateral multifocal cream seeding marks haematogenous spread; ocular therapy palliates while oncology controls primary. Solitary mushroom differs.

items.q: Port wine facial stain with tomato ketchup choroid and glaucoma is which syndrome?
o: Sturge Weber with leptomeningeal angioma and seizure watch
items.exp: Trigeminal angioma extends intracranially (tram track calcification) with choroidal haemangioma leaking; photodynamic therapy dries while neurology follows seizures.
items.kp: Port wine plus red choroid: Sturge Weber.

items.q: Retinal haemangioblastoma with dilated feeder vessels in young adult prompts hunt for what?
o: von Hippel Lindau systemic tumours (cerebellar, renal, phaeochromocytoma)
items.exp: Autosomal dominant VHL seeds retina, brain, kidneys and adrenals; laser or cryo ablates small lesions while MRI and catecholamines survey the body.
items.kp: Feeder vessel ball in youth: scan body for VHL.

items.q: Coats disease differs from retinoblastoma chiefly by which features?
o: Telangiectatic leaking vessels without calcification in older boys versus calcified tumour in toddlers
items.exp: Coats exudes lipid subretinally with light bulb aneurysms (unilateral boys); laser ablates telangiectasia while tumour protocols would overtreat massively.
items.kp: Leaking telangiectasia, no calcium, older boy: Coats.

items.q: Second tumour risk after retinoblastoma radiotherapy is classically what?
o: Osteosarcoma in irradiated field needing lifelong surveillance
items.exp: RB1 plus radiation multiplies midface sarcomas decades later; proton and chemo reduction strategies balance while MRI follows survivors.
items.kp: Irradiated RB1 child grows bone cancer later: survey.

items.q: Sentinel episcleral vessel with sectoral cataract and high pressure hints at hidden tumour of what?
o: Ciliary body melanoma compressing lens and angle
items.exp: Ciliary tumours lurk behind iris dilating episcleral channels while displacing lens; ultrasound biomicroscopy reveals while cataract surgery alone disseminates.
items.kp: Sentinel vessel plus lens shift: ciliary tumour.
